references.text: The prohibition against misusing the Lord's name is relevant here because the mother pronounces a curse (oath) in the Lord's name over the one who took the silver.
The law regarding giving testimony when hearing an oath or curse relates to the mother's curse that the son heard and responded to.
Anyone who hears a curse and does not report it bears guilt. The son confesses after hearing his mother's curse.
Curses pronounced in the Lord's name carried serious weight in Israel, which explains the son's fear and confession.
The blessing formula 'Blessed be...' used by the mother resembles Melchizedek's blessing of Abram.
